chunks: And it was narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who had never performed hajj at all, while he had wealth, so he said:
"He is among those about whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind.'"
So I said: "Glory be to Allah! Blind?"
He said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has blinded him from the path of الخير."
ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about someone who can afford hajj but never performs it?
ai.summary: This hadith warns against neglecting hajj despite having the financial means to perform it. By invoking the Quranic phrase about being raised blind on the Day of Resurrection, the Imam عليه السلام explains this as blindness from the path of goodness, showing the grave spiritual consequence of abandoning an obligatory act of worship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.2934 - It was narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who had never performed Hajj despite having wealth.
Imam (as) said: "He is among those about whom Allah (swt), the Exalted, says: 'And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind.' (Surah Ta-Ha 20:124)."
I said: "Glory be to Allah (swt)! Blind?"
Imam (as) replied: "Allah (swt), the Exalted, has blinded him from the path of goodness."
